title: A blessing for my son's wedding
titleOriginal: ڈاکٹر احمد تبسم دے گھر والے — اپنے سونہے پتر رضا علی احمد دے ویاہ اتے دعا
takeaway: A father's prayer: may every day of your life feel like Eid.
scene: This section is headed 'Dr. Ahmad Tabassum's family'. The first poem is a prayer the poet wrote for the wedding of his handsome son, Raza Ali Ahmad.

original: سدا جگ اندر خشی نال وسیں ہر روز تیرا روز عید دار ہے
رکھے غماں توں رب آزاد تینوں ساوا باغ نت تیری امید دار ہے
transliteration: Sada jag andar khushi naal vaseen, har roz tera roz-e-Eid daar hai
Rakkhe ghamaan ton Rab azaad tainu, saava baagh nit teri umeed daar hai
translation: May you always live happily in this world; may every day of yours be like the day of Eid.
May God keep you free from sorrow; may the green garden of your hopes always flourish.
couplets.story: He prays that his son will always be happy, and that every single day will feel like Eid, the happiest day of the year. He asks God to keep his son free from sadness, and to keep his hopes growing like a green garden.

original: تارا مشتری تیرا دلال بن کے تیرے واسطے خشی خرید دار ہے
چمکے تاریاں وانگ نصیب احمدؔ گھڑی پل لمحہ تیرا سعید دار ہے
transliteration: Taara Mushtari tera dalaal ban ke tere vaaste khushi khareed daar hai
Chamke taariyaan vaang naseeb Ahmad, ghari pal lamha tera saeed daar hai
translation: May the star Jupiter act as your agent and buy happiness for you.
May your fortune shine like the stars, Ahmad's son; may every hour, moment and instant of yours be blessed.
couplets.story: In old tradition, the planet Jupiter brings good luck. He jokes that Jupiter should act like a shopkeeper and 'buy' happiness for his son. May his luck shine like the stars, and may every moment of his life be blessed.

deeper: This is a father's blessing, not a mystical poem. Its faith is simple and warm: 'May God keep you free from sorrow.' The line about Jupiter buying happiness is a playful use of an old Punjabi saying, not a belief in stars.
why: A warm, simple father's blessing that anyone could use at a wedding.
prompt: If you could give someone you love one wish for their future, what would it be?
